post.description: MAZ-123. Redeems a single-use reset code: one an operator issued with the `reset-password EMAIL` maintenance command and delivered out of band, or one from the link a reset email carries (MAZ-124, POST /api/auth/password-reset/request; the link is `<Email__AppUrl>/reset-password#code=<code>`). Redeeming it stores the new password as an ASP.NET Core Identity hash and revokes every session of the account; no session is issued, so the user then signs in normally. The request names no email, so responses never reveal whether an account exists. Unknown, malformed, used, superseded and expired codes share one 400 message. Shares the sign-in rate limit; the origin policy applies. See docs/reference/authentication.md#password-reset.

200.description: Password replaced and all sessions revoked.

400.description: `This reset code is invalid or has expired.` for any unusable code, `Enter a password of 10–256 characters.` for an invalid password (the code stays usable), or `Invalid JSON.`

post.description: The request body is the file itself, 1 byte to 10 MiB (contract 2.0.0, MAZ-131). Content-Type is the file's type (case-insensitive, parameters ignored); Content-Disposition carries its name. A base64 JSON body from an older app is refused with 400 "Update Penny to upload receipts.".

post.summary: Search authorized personal entries and shared expenses (v1)
post.description: MAZ-121. Matches by title or document substring (literal, after the shared normalization), by typo (pg_trgm word_similarity) and by meaning (multilingual embeddings, at most 200 closest authorized results). Authorization runs before matching, ranking, counting and paging: the viewer's own entries and the shared expenses visible under the household-view rules; a payer's account name matches only for the payer. Receipt text (MAZ-125), extracted on the server after upload, is a separate field matched by substring, typo and meaning (its own chunk embeddings, never the entry's), only for viewers who may read the receipt; that check runs in the same statement and inside the vector index scan. A receipt matches only after its text is extracted (and, for meaning, embedded). Keyset cursors are bound to a hash of the normalized query, filters and sort. 30 requests per minute per session; 503 with Retry-After when the 2-second statement timeout fires. See docs/reference/search.md.

post.summary: Ask for a password reset email
post.description: MAZ-124. A signed-out user asks for a reset by email. The answer is 202 `{ok:true}` whether or not the address has an account, whether an earlier email is still waiting to be sent and whether the daily limits (Email__RecipientMessagesPerDay, Email__AccountMessagesPerDay) are reached: nothing tells them apart. The email is sent outside the request by the mail worker, with a link to `<Email__AppUrl>/reset-password#code=<code>`: the same single-use code as the operator command, valid for Auth__PasswordResetHours and replacing any earlier one. Redeem it with POST /api/auth/password-reset. Shares the sign-in rate limit; the origin policy applies. See docs/reference/authentication.md#password-reset-by-email.

202.description: Accepted; an email is sent if the address has an account.

400.description: `Enter a valid email address.` or `Invalid JSON.`

The invitee still joins with POST /api/households/join, so they accept it. See docs/reference/households.md#invitations-by-email.

post.summary: Verify your email with an emailed code
post.description: MAZ-172. Redeems the code from a verification email's link (`<Email__AppUrl>/verify-email#code=<code>`). Anonymous, so the link works on any device. The code is single use, expires after 48 hours, is replaced by every newer verification email and works only while the account still has the address it was sent to. Success records the email as verified (users.email_verified_at) and returns the address. Verification only records that the address is proven: nothing waits for it. Works while email is off too, for links sent before. Shares the sign-in rate limit; the origin policy applies. See docs/reference/authentication.md#email-verification-maz-172.

400.description: `This verification link is invalid or has expired.` for a missing, malformed, unknown, used, superseded or expired code, or one sent to an earlier address; or `Invalid JSON.`

post.description: MAZ-172. Queues a new verification email to the signed-in account's address. The answer is 202 `{ok:true}` whether or not an email is queued: nothing is queued for a verified account, while an earlier one is still waiting, within 60 seconds of the last one, or past the daily limits (Email__RecipientMessagesPerDay, Email__AccountMessagesPerDay). Clients count the minute down before offering Resend again. The new email's code replaces the earlier one. No request body. Shares the sign-in rate limit.

404.description: `This server doesn't send email.` while email is off: verification is off, so clients show no unverified state.

post.description: MAZ-172. A password account changes its email after confirming its password. The new address follows the sign-up rule (trimmed, lowercased, at most 254 characters). The account becomes unverified, a code sent to an earlier address stops working and, while the server sends email, a verification email goes to the new address. Sessions stay. The same address changes nothing. Returns the updated profile. Shares the sign-in rate limit.

400.description: `Enter a valid email address.`, a wrong or missing password (`Your current password is incorrect.`) or `Invalid JSON.` The session stays signed in.

403.description: Untrusted origin, or an account that signs in with a provider (`Your sign-in provider manages your email. Change it with your provider.`).

post.description: MAZ-152. Deletes the signed-in account after checking its password, and signs out every device, this one included (the session cookie is cleared). Rate-limited like sign-in. The person leaves every household they're in under the rules for leaving: settled in every month, and a creator only when no other member remains. Deleted: the personal ledger (entries, accounts, categories, schedules, trips), receipts and their text, emailed receipts and the receipt email address, search documents, sessions, push devices, pending email and push messages, the picture, the name and the email. Kept for the other members: shared expenses with their splits and payments, shared schedules and the household history, with the person shown as a former member (`deleted` on HouseholdMember); their receipts and account names are removed from those expenses. Backups keep deleted data until they age out (docs/self-hosting).

400.description: A wrong or missing password ("Your password is incorrect."). Nothing is deleted and the session stays.

409.description: A household rule blocks leaving, and nothing is deleted: "Settle every monthly balance in <household> before you delete your account." or "You created <household>, and other people are still in it. Remove them or archive <household> before you delete your account."

get.description: MAZ-152. One ZIP file (`penny-export-YYYY-MM-DD.zip`) with everything on the server that belongs to the signed-in person. JSON files use this contract's shapes: `README.txt`; `profile.json` (`profile`: Profile, `name` and `picture` with `managedBy` "you" or "signInProvider", and the picture's file); `profile/picture.webp` when there is a picture; `ledger.json` (Snapshot); `entries.csv` (as /api/export/entries for everything); `households/NN-name.json` for every household and trip joined, archived ones too (`household`, `members`, `expenses` the person can see with everyone's share, `recurring`, `history`); `receipts/<id>-<name>` for each receipt they uploaded, as the original file. The server writes the ZIP to a temporary file and deletes it when the download ends.

200.description: The ZIP file, as an attachment.

get.description: MAZ-152. Personal entries and the person's share of recorded shared expenses for a month, a year or everything, oldest first, as a CSV file (`penny-entries-<period>.csv`, or the day's date for everything) that spreadsheets open as is: UTF-8 with a byte order mark, CRLF line ends, RFC 4180 quoting. Columns: Date, Type (Expense, Income or Investment), Title, Category, Account, Amount, Your share (positive decimals), Currency, Household (shared expenses), Trip, Note. Text that a spreadsheet would read as a formula starts with an apostrophe.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: A month (YYYY-MM). Takes precedence over year.

200.description: The CSV file, as an attachment.

400.description: An invalid month ("Invalid household data.") or year ("Invalid year.").

post.summary: Send web error, performance and replay reports
post.description: MAZ-129. Opt-in client telemetry, forwarded to the operator collector on a private network after a schema check, server-side scrubbing (URLs keep only their path shape; emails, quoted text and numbers in messages are redacted) and duplicate filtering. Never carries ledger contents, titles, notes, amounts, emails or search text. Available when /api/info telemetry.web is true.

parameters.description: 8 to 64 letters, digits, - or _. A key the same user sent in the last ten minutes is accepted again (202) without forwarding.

schema.description: A Grafana Faro Web SDK request body. meta.app.name must be penny-web; meta.user and meta.geo are dropped. Session Replay events (faro.session_recording.*) are re-masked, or dropped when telemetry.sessionReplay is false.

webhookSignature.name: X-Penny-Signature
webhookSignature.description:
MAZ-184: lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 with InboundMail__WebhookSecret over `penny/inbound-mail/v1
<purpose>
<X-Penny-Timestamp>
<subject>
<sha256(body) hex>`. Purpose `message` (subject: X-Penny-Recipient) or `recipients` (subject: the request path). Timestamps more than 5 minutes off are refused. Used only by the Cloudflare Email Worker (apps/email-worker).

Error.description: Every error response. `error` is the English message the apps show; `code` (contract 2.1.0) is a stable machine-readable name for the failure, so a client can branch on it instead of on the status or the text. A code never changes meaning, and new codes may be added: treat an unknown code like its status. Servers before contract 2.1.0 send `error` only. See docs/reference/api-reference.md#error-codes.

token.description: The 64-character lowercase hex reset code: issued by the operator, or carried by the emailed link (MAZ-124).

Me.description: Who is signed in, with the profile summary the apps' chrome shows (MAZ-171). This server always sends userId and needsName, and displayName and avatarUrl when present; servers before profiles send only email, so clients treat them as optional. Profile has the editable flags.

displayName.description: Omitted when the person has none: show the email. Display text only, never identity: trimmed, 1-60 UTF-16 units, no control characters or line and paragraph separators.

avatarUrl.description: Omitted when the person has no picture: show initials. Same-origin URL of the picture (a square WebP of at most 512 px). Load it with the session; the version changes with every picture, so a URL may be cached for good.

needsName.description: True when the apps should ask for a name (no name, editable, prompt not dismissed). Skipping sends namePromptDismissed.

deleted.description: MAZ-152. Present (true) when the person deleted their account: show "Former member" and never the email, which is a placeholder address. Their expenses, splits and payments stay, so balances don't change. Omitted otherwise.

date.description: Local calendar date; valid dates are 2000-01-01 through 2100-12-31.
Local calendar date; valid dates are 2000-01-01 through 2100-12-31.
Local calendar date; valid dates are 2000-01-01 through 2100-12-31.

ExpensePayer.description: Who paid a shared expense, as the household members see them (MAZ-275).

displayName.description: The payer's display name (MAZ-171). Omitted when they have none: show the email.

deleted.description: MAZ-152. Present (true) when the person deleted their account: show "Former member" and never the email, which is a placeholder address. Their expenses, splits and payments stay, so balances don't change. Omitted otherwise.

date.description: Local calendar date; valid dates are 2000-01-01 through 2100-12-31.

paidByYou.description: True when the viewer paid. Clients say "You paid" rather than the payer's name.

recurringId.description: The shared rule: on previews (`scheduled: true`) and, since MAZ-139, on recorded occurrences the rule recorded. Omitted for one-off expenses. Clients match a recorded row to a cached preview by householdId, recurringId and date.

nextDate.description: Local calendar date; valid dates are 2000-01-01 through 2100-12-31.
Local calendar date; valid dates are 2000-01-01 through 2100-12-31.
Local calendar date; valid dates are 2000-01-01 through 2100-12-31.

anchorDay.description: Present on list/read responses; create/update currently echo the request without this field.

PushDevice.description: A native iOS APNs registration: a hex device token with provider "apns", platform "ios" and the APNs environment that issued it. Any other provider or platform is refused with 400. Unknown keys are ignored.

privacyPolicyUrl.description: The server operator's privacy policy (Legal__PrivacyPolicyUrl), an absolute http or https URL. Null when the server publishes none, and absent from servers older than this field: clients then show no privacy policy link. Clients open it in the browser.

emailEnabled.description: MAZ-124. Whether the server sends email (Email__Smtp__Host is set). When true, clients offer password reset by email and invitations by email; when false, or absent on servers older than this field, they fall back to codes: an operator-issued reset code and shared invite codes.

query.description: Trimmed (ECMAScript trim), then at most 200 UTF-16 code units. Empty matches everything that passes the filters.

from.description: Inclusive first calendar date. Omitting from and to searches all time.

to.description: Inclusive last calendar date; not before from.

kind.description: Default: every kind. Shared expenses are expenses.

sort.description: Default relevance for a non-empty query, otherwise date-desc (relevance with an empty query is date-desc). Amount sorts use the viewer's share. Every sort ends with date descending, then key ascending.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor of the previous page; 400 when it belongs to another query, filter or sort.

SearchRequest.description: Search v1. Real calendar dates from 2000-01-01 to 2100-12-31 and from <= to are enforced by the service; unknown fields are rejected. The viewer is always the session's user.

match.description: Best matching tier; null for an empty query.
Best matching tier; null for an empty query.

totalCount.description: Authorized matching results, each counted once (meaning matches only within the 200-result cap). Not a money total.

ReceiptEmailAddress.description: A live private receipt address (MAZ-184). Times are Unix milliseconds.

allowedSenders.description: Lowercase addresses or domains. Empty: any sender.

ReceiptEmail.description: Whether this server accepts emailed receipts, its receipt domain, and the user's live address (MAZ-184).

ReceiptEmailUpdate.description: At least one of: extend (restart the lifetime from now), allowedSenders (replace the list).

InboundRecipients.description: SHA-256 hex of each live receipt address local part, sorted, for the Email Worker (MAZ-184). No user ids or expiry dates.

ReceiptInboxFile.description: One file of an inbox item: the rendered email or an imported attachment. Download it from uri (GET /api/receipts/{id}); attach it with the normal entry or shared expense save.

linked.description: An entry, live shared expense or shared rule links it.

ReceiptInboxItem.description: One received email in the owner-only receipt inbox (MAZ-184). from and subject are plain text: never interpret them as HTML or Markdown. Times are Unix milliseconds.

senderVerified.description: The sender domain passed DMARC at Penny ingress. Show Sender not verified when false.

expiresAt.description: When an unhandled item is discarded. Null once attached.

next.description: Pass as before for the next page.

ReceiptInboxCleanup.description: Files deleted, and files kept because something links them.

Registration.description: Credentials plus the optional name asked at sign-up (MAZ-171). Older apps send only the credentials; a blank displayName counts as none.

displayName.description: Optional. When not blank, the same rules as Profile.displayName (400 otherwise).

Profile.description: The signed-in person's profile (MAZ-171). Only people who share a household or trip with them see their name and picture (on HouseholdMember).

displayName.description: Omitted when the person has none: show the email. Display text only, never identity: trimmed, 1-60 UTF-16 units, no control characters or line and paragraph separators.

avatarUrl.description: Omitted when the person has no picture: show initials. Same-origin URL of the picture (a square WebP of at most 512 px). Load it with the session; the version changes with every picture, so a URL may be cached for good.

nameEditable.description: False when the sign-in provider sends the name: it is read only and refreshed at each sign-in.

avatarEditable.description: False when the sign-in provider sends the picture: it is read only and refreshed at each sign-in.

needsName.description: True when the apps should ask for a name (no name, editable, prompt not dismissed). Skipping sends namePromptDismissed.

signIn.description: How the account signs in. An account has exactly one sign-in method.

provider.description: For an oidc account: the configured display name of its own sign-in provider, found by the account's issuer. Omitted when not configured; say "your sign-in provider".

passwordChangedAt.description: Unix milliseconds when a password account last changed its password (signed in or by reset). Omitted before the first change and for oidc accounts.

emailVerified.description: MAZ-172. Whether the account's current email is proven: an emailed link was opened, the sign-in provider says so, an operator marked it, or the account existed before email verification. Nothing waits for it. Show the unverified state and Resend only while the server sends email (`emailEnabled` on /api/info).

emailVerifiedAt.description: MAZ-172. Unix milliseconds when the current email was verified. Omitted while unverified.

providerId.description: MAZ-170. For an oidc account: the `id` of its configured provider in `GET /api/auth/oidc`. Omitted when not configured.

providerIcon.description: MAZ-170. For an oidc account: the `icon` of its configured provider. Omitted when not configured.

displayName.description: A name (the Profile.displayName rules, 400 otherwise) or null to clear it so the email shows. 403 when the provider manages the name.

namePromptDismissed.description: The person skipped the name prompt; needsName becomes false.

EmailInvite.description: MAZ-124. An invitation sent by email. The address is normalized (trimmed, lower case).

status.description: `sending`: queued, or a resend not yet sent. `waiting`: sent, unused and unexpired. `expired`: its code expired. `joined`: someone joined with it. `failed`: the mail server refused it for good.

sentAt.description: When its latest email was sent, Unix milliseconds.

expiresAt.description: When the emailed code stops working (Email__InviteHours after sending), Unix milliseconds; null before the first email and after joining.

EmailVerified.description: The address an emailed link verified (MAZ-172).

EmailChange.description: A signed-in email change for a password account (MAZ-172).

AccountDeletion.description: MAZ-152. Confirms deleting the signed-in account.

password.description: The account's password. Required for password accounts (`signIn: password` on Profile); an account that signs in with a provider has none and sends `{}`.

ClientTelemetryInfo.description: MAZ-129. Which opt-in client telemetry the server accepts (ClientTelemetry__*). Absent on older servers: clients then treat every flag as false and never ask, collect or send.

web.description: The web app may offer error and performance reports (ClientTelemetry__FaroUrl is set).

sessionReplay.description: The web app may also offer Session Replay, with every text and field masked (ClientTelemetry__SessionReplay).

native.description: The iOS app may offer crash and performance reports (ClientTelemetry__OtlpEndpoint is set).
